title: And Can My Heart Aspire So High
description: And Can My Heart Aspire So High in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 481 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Filial Submission”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And can my heart as-pire so high, To say, "My Fa-ther," God? Lord, at thy feet, I fain would lie, And learn to kiss the rod.

lines: And can my heart aspire so high,
Lord, at thy feet, I fain would lie,
And learn to kiss the rod.
I would submit to all thy will,
For thou art good and wise;
Let each rebellious thought be still,
Thy love can cheer the darkest gloom,
Till hopes and joys immortal bloom,
And ask the bliss those words impart,

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
